newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bomb wounds two SLA militiamen in south Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Bomb wounds two SLA militiamen in south Lebanon.

text.p: A roadside bomb wounded two Israeli-allied South Lebanon Army (SLA) militiamen in south Lebanon late on Wednesday, SLA sources said.
The sources said one of the men was seriously injured.
In Beirut, the pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) said it planted the bomb in the Jezzine area which is officially outside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone but under Israeli and SLA control.
"The Islamic resistance detonated a roadside bomb targeting a motorcade belonging to SLA agent Emile Nasr, leader of the 20th brigade of the SLA," said a Hizbollah spokesman.
The SLA sources said the bombing was followed by retaliatory Israeli shelling north of Jezzine.
The 3,000-strong SLA militia helps some 1,000 Israeli troops hold a 15-km (nine-miles)-deep occupation zone in south Lebanon to protect northern Israel from guerrilla attacks.
Hizbollah frequently attacks Israeli and SLA posts and patrols in a bid to drive the Israelis from the occupation zone.
